page: Amazon Web Services m7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions for accelerated mathematical and matrix operations.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core capabilities, with the server achieving top-tier placement in Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core tests. It demonstrates high-throughput memory performance, recording a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 231.55 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 95.32 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing performance is notable, as evidenced by a top-tier Passmark CPU encryption score. Additionally, the platform delivers strong performance in database operations, static web serving, and LLM inference prompt processing across small, medium, and large models.

The server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps but lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware. This makes it reliant on network-attached storage for persistent data. Given its high core density and balanced memory allocation, the m7i.metal-24xl is qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale enterprise workloads that require direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. It is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
